says.detail:
This page is about the Health Board complaints process, not a compensation scheme. It says to raise the complaint as soon as possible or within a year in some cases, the Health Board processes the complaint and aims to respond within 30 working days, but it does not mention compensation, legal advice, court rights, a cap, or a separate decision-maker for compensation.
Quotes: "If you are unhappy with the treatment or care you are receiving, we would encourage you to raise your complaint as soon as possible" | "Other than in exceptional circumstances, a complaint should be made as quickly as possible in relation to the problem arising." | "as long as no more than a year has passed." | "The aim is for you to receive a written response to your complaint within 30 working days."

says.text: For this kind of Wales NHS case, the practical route is to start with a complaint to Cardiff and Vale University Health Board, because that can lead to NHS redress and, if redress is considered, paid legal advice within the scheme. Ordinary clinical-negligence legal aid is not the main route here, so if the case needs to go outside NHS redress, it is likely to be through a no win, no fee claimant solicitor. I could not safely shortlist firms because the official Law Society directory was blocked by a CAPTCHA and I did not get firm names back to verify.

scheme.body: Welsh NHS redress scheme under the National Health Service (Concerns, Complaints and Redress Arrangements) (Wales) Regulations
scheme.text: This page is about the Health Board complaints process, not a compensation scheme. It says to raise the complaint as soon as possible or within a year in some cases, the Health Board processes the complaint and aims to respond within 30 working days, but it does not mention compensation, legal advice, court rights, a cap, or a separate decision-maker for compensation.
